trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, DAKSHINA KANNADA, MANGALURU, MC.NO.144/2018
case_name: Mr Nithyananda Rai vs Mrs Soumya
facts_of_case: The parties were married under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court dismissed the petition filed by the husband under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife had filed a counter-claim for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A petition for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 can be allowed if the respondent has failed to perform their marital obligations.
legal_principles.held: It is held that the counter-claim of the respondent under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 was allowed as the respondent had failed to perform her marital obligations and the appellant had not been able to live with her for a long time.

legal_principles.principle: A court can allow a counter-claim for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 if the respondent has failed to perform their marital obligations.
legal_principles.held: This Court holds that the counter-claim of the respondent was allowed as she had failed to perform her marital obligations and the appellant had not been able to live with her for a long time.

outcome.final_order: The appeals are dismissed as withdrawn. The pending interlocutory application is also dismissed.
